ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: The idea that we are living moments of more and lives of less is supported by a recent study in which pairs of college-aged friends were asked to communicate in four different ways: face-to-face conversation, video chat, audio chat, and online instant messaging. Then, the degree of emotional bonding in these friendships was assessed both by asking how people felt and watching how they behaved toward each other. The results were clear: In-person conversation led to the most emotional connection and online messaging led to the least. The students had tried to "warm up" their digital messages by using emoticons, typing out the sounds of laughter ("Hahaha"), and using the forced urgency of TYPING IN ALL CAPS. But these techniques had not done the job. It is when we see each other's faces and hear each other's voices that we become most human to each other.

questions.passage: The idea that we are living moments of more and lives of less is (A)[opposed / supported] by a recent study in which pairs of college-aged friends were asked to communicate in four different ways: face-to-face conversation, video chat, audio chat, and online instant messaging. Then, the degree of emotional bonding in these friendships was (B)[assessed / ignored] both by asking how people felt and watching how they behaved toward each other. The results were (C)[clear / unclear]: In-person conversation led to the most emotional connection and online messaging led to the least. The students had tried to "warm up" their digital messages by using emoticons, typing out the sounds of laughter ("Hahaha"), and using the forced urgency of TYPING IN ALL CAPS. But these techniques had not done the job. It is when we see each other's faces and hear each other's voices that we become most human to each other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① supported — assessed — clear: 그 생각은 최근 연구로 '뒷받침되고', 정서적 유대는 '평가되었으며', 결과는 '명확'했다.
❌ ② opposed — assessed — clear: (A) 연구가 그 생각을 '반박'한 것이 아니라 '뒷받침'함.
❌ ③ supported — ignored — clear: (B) 유대를 '무시'한 것이 아니라 '평가'함.
❌ ④ supported — assessed — unclear: (C) 결과는 '불명확'이 아니라 '명확'했음.

questions.passage: The idea that we are living moments of more and lives of less is supported by a recent study in which pairs of college-aged friends were asked to (A)[compete / communicate] in four different ways: face-to-face conversation, video chat, audio chat, and online instant messaging. Then, the degree of emotional bonding in these friendships was assessed both by asking how people felt and watching how they behaved toward each other. The results were clear: In-person conversation led to the most emotional (B)[connection / distance] and online messaging led to the (C)[least / most]. The students had tried to "warm up" their digital messages by using emoticons, typing out the sounds of laughter ("Hahaha"), and using the forced urgency of TYPING IN ALL CAPS. But these techniques had not done the job. It is when we see each other's faces and hear each other's voices that we become most human to each other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 의사소통하다(communicate), 연결(connection), 가장 적은(least)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ communicate — connection — least: 친구들은 네 가지 방식으로 '의사소통'했고, 대면은 가장 큰 정서적 '연결'을, 온라인은 '가장 적은' 연결을 낳았다.
❌ ① compete — connection — least: (A) '경쟁'이 아니라 '의사소통'하도록 요청받음.
❌ ② communicate — distance — least: (B) 대면이 가장 큰 '거리'가 아니라 '연결'을 낳음.
❌ ④ communicate — connection — most: (C) 온라인 메시지는 '가장 많은'이 아니라 '가장 적은' 연결.
det.tip: led to the most ~ / led to the least ~ = 가장 많은 ~ / 가장 적은 ~을 낳다

The results were clear: In-person conversation led to the most emotional connection and online messaging led to the least. The students had tried to "warm up" their digital messages by using emoticons, typing out the sounds of laughter ("Hahaha"), and using the (A)[genuine / forced] urgency of TYPING IN ALL CAPS. But these (B)[techniques / feelings] had not done the job. It is when we see each other's faces and hear each other's voices that we become most (C)[human / distant] to each other.

det.analysis:
✅ ④ forced — techniques — human: 대문자 입력은 '억지스러운' 긴박감을 주고, 이런 '기법'들은 효과가 없었으며, 얼굴을 볼 때 가장 '인간적'이 된다.
❌ ① forced — techniques — distant: (C) 서로 '멀어지는'이 아니라 가장 '인간적'이 됨.
❌ ② forced — feelings — human: (B) '감정'이 아니라 이런 '기법'들이 효과가 없었음.
❌ ③ genuine — techniques — human: (A) 대문자의 긴박감은 '진짜'가 아니라 '억지스러운' 것.
det.tip: forced urgency = 억지스러운(인위적인) 긴박감, become most human = 가장 인간적이 되다

questions.passage: Pairs of college-aged friends were asked to communicate in four different ways. Then, the degree of emotional bonding was measured both by asking how people felt and __________ how they behaved toward each other. (watch)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: watch → watching: 앞의 asking과 병렬을 이루는 동명사 (관찰하는 것).
det.analysis: 'both by asking ... and __________ ...' 구조에서 앞의 동명사 asking과 병렬을 이루어야 하므로 watching. watch → watching.
det.tip: both by A and B 병렬: asking ~ and watching ~ (동명사 병렬)

questions.passage: The idea that we are living moments of more and lives of less is supported by a recent study in which pairs of college-aged friends were asked to communicate in four different ways: face-to-face conversation, video chat, audio chat, and online instant messaging. Then, the degree of emotional bonding in these friendships was assessed both by asking how people felt and watching how they behaved toward each other. The results were clear: In-person conversation led to the most emotional connection and online messaging led to the least. The students had tried to "warm up" their digital messages by using emoticons, typing out the sounds of laughter ("Hahaha"), and using the forced urgency of TYPING IN ALL CAPS. But these techniques had not __________. It is when we see each other's faces and hear each other's voices that we become most human to each other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: done the job (제 역할을 하다): 그 기법들은 '효과를 내지' 못했습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② done the job: 'do the job'은 '제 역할을 하다, 효과를 내다'라는 뜻. 뒤 문장(얼굴을 봐야 인간적이 됨)과 대조되어 기법들이 '효과가 없었다'는 흐름과 일치.
❌ ① broken the rules: '규칙을 어기다'는 문맥과 무관.
❌ ③ lost the game: '경기에서 지다'는 비유가 부적절.
❌ ④ missed the point: '요점을 놓치다'는 유사해 보이나 기법의 '효과 없음'을 나타내는 서술과 결이 다름.
det.tip: do the job = 제 역할을 하다, 효과를 내다

questions.passage: The idea that we are living moments of more and lives of less is supported by a recent study in which pairs of college-aged friends were asked to communicate in four different ways: face-to-face conversation, video chat, audio chat, and online instant messaging. Then, the degree of emotional bonding in these friendships was assessed both by asking how people felt and watching how they behaved toward each other. The results were clear: In-person conversation led to the most emotional connection and online messaging led to the least. The students had tried to "warm up" their digital messages by using emoticons, typing out the sounds of laughter ("Hahaha"), and using the forced urgency of TYPING IN ALL CAPS. But these techniques had not done the job. It is when we see each other's faces and hear each other's voices that we become most __________ to each other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: human (인간적인): 얼굴을 보고 목소리를 들을 때 서로에게 가장 '인간적'이 됩니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ human: 대면 소통이 정서적 유대를 높인다는 글의 핵심. 얼굴을 보고 목소리를 들을 때 서로에게 가장 '인간적'인 존재가 됨.
❌ ① distant: '먼, 소원한'은 글의 주제(대면이 유대를 높임)와 정반대.
❌ ② formal: '격식 있는'은 정서적 유대 문맥과 무관.
❌ ③ similar: '비슷한'은 문맥상 부적절.
det.tip: become most human to each other = 서로에게 가장 인간적인 존재가 되다
